title: Temporary Executive Assistant / Administrator
description:
Temporary Executive Assistant / Administrator

Location: Twickenham
Duration: 4-8 Weeks
Start Date: ASAP
Contract Type: Temporary

Overview

Our client is seeking an experienced and highly organised Temporary Executive Assistant / Administrator to provide a blend of executive support and office administration. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and can quickly adapt to new systems and processes.

The role is split approximately 50/50 between supporting the Manager and providing general office administration support.

Key Responsibilities
Executive Assistant Support
- Manage the Manager's diary and calendar, ensuring schedules are effectively coordinated.
- Arrange and coordinate meetings, including sending invitations and managing meeting logistics.
- Monitor and manage email inboxes, prioritising correspondence and responding where appropriate.
- Act as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders.
- Provide general administrative support to the Manager as required.

Administration & Office Support
- Manage incoming emails through a ticketing system, ensuring requests are allocated to the appropriate teams for action.
- Monitor ticket progress and assist with follow-up where necessary.
- Maintain accurate records and update internal systems.
- Support day-to-day office administration activities.
- Assist with document management, filing and general business support tasks.
- Collaborate with colleagues to ensure smooth operational processes.

Skills & Experience Required
- Previous experience in an Executive Assistant, Personal Assistant, Office Administrator or similar support role.
- Strong organisational and time management skills.
- Experience managing busy calendars and coordinating meetings.
- Confident handling multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- High attention to detail and ability to work independently.

Systems Experience
- HubSpot (essential)
- Microsoft Outlook (essential)
- Experience working with ticketing or workflow management systems would be advantageous.

Person Specification
- Proactive and self-sufficient approach to work.
- Strong problem-solving abilities.
- Professional and approachable manner.
- Able to hit the ground running with minimal supervision.
- Flexible and adaptable to changing priorities.

What's on Offer
- Immediate start available.
- Short-term temporary assignment (4-8 weeks).
- Varied role combining EA and administrative responsibilities.
- Opportunity to gain experience within a dynamic business environment.

Interested candidates should be available to start immediately and commit to the duration of the assignment.

title: Sales Administrator
description:
Sales Administrator

The Company

Our client is a well-established company supplying branded products to businesses across the UK. They have built an excellent reputation for quality and service and continue to grow, working with a wide range of clients.

They are now looking for a friendly, organised and proactive Sales Administrator to join their team.

The Role

This is a varied role that combines sales administration, customer service and basic accounts. You will be looking after existing customer accounts, processing orders, completing general administration and assisting with the day-to-day accounts function using Sage.

You ll also have the opportunity to build relationships with customers and, where appropriate, visit clients. There is also the potential to earn commission.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing and developing existing customer accounts.
- Processing customer enquiries, quotations and sales orders.
- Speaking with customers over the phone and providing excellent customer service.
- Using the company CRM system to manage customer information and orders.
- Raising sales invoices.
- Processing purchase invoices.
- Assisting with general accounts administration using Sage.
- Maintaining accurate customer and sales records.
- Liaising with suppliers and internal departments.
- Visiting clients when opportunities arise.
- Supporting the wider office team with general administration.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will have:
- Previous experience in a Sales Administrator, Office Administrator or Customer Service role.
- Basic accounts experience, including purchase and sales invoicing.
- Experience using Sage or similar accounting software.
- Experience using a CRM system.
- Confident and professional telephone manner.
- Excellent communication and organisational skills.
- Good attention to detail.
- A positive, flexible and team-oriented approach.
- Good knowledge of Microsoft Office.

Salary & Benefits
- £27,000 £33,000 per annum, depending on experience.
- Opportunity to visit clients and build long-term relationships.
- Join a friendly, growing business where your contribution is valued.

If you re looking for a varied role where no two days are the same and you enjoy working with customers while supporting sales and accounts, we d love to hear from you.

Application Process

Due to the high volume of applications received, Aspire Recruitment Consultants will only contact candidates who have been shortlisted for this position.

If you do not hear from us, please assume your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion. However, we encourage you to apply for future opportunities and thank you for your interest in the role.

title: HR Assistant
description:
Job Title: HR Assistant/PA to the Headteacher

Hours: 17.5 hours per week

Reporting to: Operations Manager/The Headteacher

Contract type: 08:00 to 12 noon Mon to Fri - Term time only

Main purpose:

As the HR Assistant, you will play a key role in ensuring HR processes run efficiently and in line with school policies and safeguarding requirements. You will manage HR administration, support recruitment processes, and maintain accurate staff records.

Duties and responsibilities:

Human Resources
- Maintaining accurate and confidential HR records e.g. staff files, contracts, DBS, absence records.
- Supporting the recruitment process including preparing job adverts, collating applications,arranging interviews, and onboarding.
- Processing starters, leavers, and contract variations.
- Assisting with the administration of payroll changes and liaising with payroll providers as necessary.
- Supporting induction and training records for staff.
- Managing staff absence returns and maintaining the Single Central Record (SCR).
- Assisting in staff communications and providing general HR-related advice and support under the guidance of the Operations Manager.
- Ensuring HR processes and data handling comply with safeguarding, confidentiality, and 0 GDPR policies.

Personal Assistant (PA)
- Manage the Headteacher's diary, ensuring effective communication and coordination.
- Maintain staff supervision records and ensure they are carried out on time.
- Provide comprehensive administrative support to the Headteacher.

General Administration
- Respond to telephone enquiries, directing queries appropriately to relevant staff members.
- Handling reprographic tasks and providing general administrative support within the school office.

Other Duties/Responsibilities:
- Be a proactive member of the Operations team.
- Attend staff meetings, appraisals, and professional development activities.
- Support general office administration duties as appropriate to the post.
- Contribute to whole school development plans and maintain high standards in daily duties.

Qualifications, Knowledge and Skills:
- A good standard of general education (GCSEs & A-Levels) or relevant vocational qualifications.
- Previous experience of working in an educational setting (desirable but not essential depending on experience).

Knowledge and Skills:
- Discretion and ability to maintain confidentiality in all HR matters.
- Understanding and commitment to safeguarding and data protection.
- Excellent analytical and data extraction skills.
- Ability to manage pressure and maintain a positive, solution-focused attitude.
- Strong numeracy and attention to detail.
- Ability to take initiative and manage workload independently.
- Strong interpersonal and team-working skills.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise effectively.
- Integrity, professionalism, and commitment to the school's vision.
- Prior experience in finance and administration (education sector experience desirable).
- Proficiency in accounting software (FMS desirable), and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook).
- Experience using HR systems or databases desirable but training can be given.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Understanding of HR policies and best practices.

title: Training Coordinator
description:
Position: Training Coordinator (Events)

Hours: 9am-5pm, Monday to Friday

Location: London Bridge / Hybrid working

About Us

At the Knowledge Exchange Group, we don't just talk about the issues shaping UK public policy - we get the right people in the room to solve them. Across our three brands, Westminster Insight, Holyrood Insight, and Policy Wales, we deliver over 100 conferences and 150 training courses a year, giving public sector and policy professionals the insight, tools, and connections they need to make a real difference. Our client list speaks for itself - from government departments and public sector bodies to charities doing genuinely meaningful work, right through to some of the biggest household names in UK private industry.

If you are highly organised, love the buzz of bringing people together and want a role where every project is different, keep reading.

The Role

We're looking for a Training Coordinator to join our fast-paced, friendly events team - someone who thrives on organisation, enjoys a full inbox, and gets a real kick out of seeing a training course come together from a blank page to course full of engaged delegates.

Whether it's a small, focused workshop of 5 or a full course of 30, our training courses are designed to engage every delegate.You'll be working closely with our Director and the marketing, product, and operations teams to make sure every course lands well, and appeals to a mix of clients.

No two days will look the same, and while some experience in event coordination is great, what matters most is your drive, your eye for detail, your passion for good customer experience, and solid negotiation and organisational skills. We'll provide full training and teach you the rest.

What You'll Be Doing
- Building and nurturing relationships with trainers and industry bodies
- Negotiating trainer fees and keeping projects on budget
- Working with trainers to shape course content - chasing bios, materials, logos and slides
- Building course websites and email campaigns
- Coordinating pre-event questionnaires to keep content sharp and relevant
- Securing CPD certification for our courses
- Supporting delegates - joining instructions, tech troubleshooting, and friendly customer service
- Gathering feedback and evaluation post-course to keep raising the bar
- Handling cost and invoice admin
- Liaising directly with clients on bespoke in-house training

About You
- At least a year's experience in a professional environment
- Some background in events or training
- Confident with everyday tech - Microsoft Office, Zoom, email systems, etc.
- Sharp organisational skills - checking the details, meeting multiple deadlines
- Experience with email marketing or website builders is a bonus
- A natural at customer service - warm, helpful, and solutions-focused
- Comfortable negotiating and thinking commercially
- A calm problem-solver who takes things in their stride
- A genuine team player who builds relationships easily
- A clear, confident communicator

What You'll Get
- 23 days' annual holiday, rising to 25 after 2 years and 28 after 3
- 2 dedicated personal development days plus access to CPD-accredited training
- Company pension scheme
- Regular company social events
- Hybrid working
- A genuinely dynamic, supportive, and agile team to be part of
- Progression within the role and the company.

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description:
Step Into Education That Truly Changes Lives

Location: Cumnor House School
Job Title: Receptionist/Administrator
Contract: Permanent, Full-Time 52 Weeks Per Year
Hours: 40 hours per week
Salary: Up to 27,000 Per Annum (depending on experience)
Start Date: End of September 2026

About Cumnor House

Here at Cumnor House , we are dedicated to giving our children the perfect platform to achieve their potential. Our philosophy is to ensure that each pupil at Cumnor House is given the opportunity to develop not just on an educational level, but also socially. Therefore, our curriculum contains varied subjects and activities, ensuring that every child gets the most out of the time they spend at school.
By striking the perfect balance between disciplined learning practices and a friendly atmosphere we can be confident in providing the perfect environment for our children to flourish.

Role Purpose

To provide support and administration services for Cumnor House Schools. Offering practical and effective solutions to day-to-day functions of the front of house and any administration duties quickly, decisively, calmly, and professionally, including travelling between school sites to support when required. Provide support to the Senior Leadership Team in ensuring all relevant parties are informed and supporting the admin team.

What you will be doing

Key Responsibilities
- Ensuring all visitors, contractors etc. are greeted professionally and that the necessary security and safety procedures are followed.
- To manage responses to parental enquiries and provide excellent customer service
- Answering telephone calls/emails and dealing with queries in a prompt and professional manner.
- Record and maintain attendance registers using the schools preferred Management Information System.
- Manage pupils' needs when they come to the reception area at various key points in the day including early morning transport shuttles between sites
- To work with others to introduce and improve procedures and processes.
- Work collaboratively with the other members of the Admin Team to provide general administration of wraparound care and school bus service, including the Parent Portal (Blenheim Connect), payment systems and various platforms to support school operations.
- Provide admin/secretarial support to SLT and other staff as required.
- Be the first point of contact to support parents with the Parent Portal (Blenheim Connect).
- Transport bookings for trips and visits.
- Responsible for working with admissions team ensuring accurate and timely processing of all data of new students.To assist the Designated Safeguarding Lead with administration as and when required.
- To provide cover for administration colleagues' absences, including travelling to any of the Cumnor sites to undertake the cover requirement.

o What you'll bring
- Literate & numerate, GCSE or equivalent Grade C in English & Maths minimum.
- Proactive and positive can-do attitude
- Ability to build and maintain excellent working relationships.
- Proficient knowledge of Microsoft packages: Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook.
- Strong administration & organisational skills (accurate and meticulous attention to detail grammatically & numerically).
- Significant experience of working in an administrative role within a busy office environment and educational settings.
- Excellent customer-facing and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to work calmly under pressure adapt effectively to changing circumstances/situations whilst remaining firm and fair.
- Excellent people skills - confident & friendly with a good awareness of customer care.
- Excellent telephone manner.
- Reliable and flexible with ways of working, including covering any of the school sites if required.
- Able to show initiative and provide attention to time critical duties.

Desirable
- First Aid qualification
- Experience of working in a busy school environment, or relevant experience in children's settings

We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications.

title: Receptionist
description: Earl's Court Medical Centre has an exciting opportunity for a Medical Receptionist to join our welcoming and forward thinking Practice team on a full-time and part-time basis. Your normal pattern of working will be Monday - Friday, within the hours of 8am-6:30pm. Interested applicants must have primary care and SystmOne experience. Key Responsibilities include: Greeting and assisting patients at the reception desk Managing appointments, cancellations and patients enquiries Answering telephone calls and directing queries appropriately Processing repeat prescription requests Supporting the administrative and clinical team with day-to-day tasks Maintaining confidentially and ensuring accurate record- keeping Processing ingoing and outgoing patient records This is a patient facing role that requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and a calm, efficient approach to working in a fast-paced environment. Reception duties: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 72 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. (including computerised practice notes), ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables (including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc.). Premises: Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Make and serve refreshments for meetings, ensure the kitchen is kept clean and tidy and air and tidy the waiting room in turn with other staff. Covering colleagues holiday and sick cover as required. Process incoming and outgoing mail according to practice protocols. Record actions taken in patient record where appropriate or in accordance with practice protocols. Complete other Daily/ Weekly and Monthly core tasks to support to smooth running of the reception area Any other administration duties as necessitated by the needs of the practice. Confidentiality : In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Act as Chaperone when requested by clinician and in accordance with the Chaperone policy. Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with the Practice policies and procedures, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of their own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for their own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality : The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication : The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: The Links Medical Practice is a GP Practice that operates from 2 sites in the Borough of Bromley. An excellent opportunity has arisen for a highly motivated individual to join our friendly Reception/Administrative team for 37.5 hours per week. The position is permanent Full Time. Hours of work range between 7:45am - 6:45pm Monday to Friday. The applicant will be based at our Mottingham site - 198 Court Farm Road, London, SE9 4JS, may also be required to work at the Downham site - 27 Brook Lane, Bromley, BR1 4PX The successful applicant will play a key role in delivering high-quality patient services, helping to ensure excellent standards of patient care and a positive experience for patients. The ideal candidate will have excellent interpersonal and communication skills, administrative abilities, and a proactive, reliable work ethic. The ability to work effectively as part of a busy team while maintaining professionalism and confidentiality is essential. Previous experience working in a GP practice is desirable. They will play a key role in ensuring patients receive the highest standard of customer care while supporting the smooth running of the practice. Welcome and assist patients and visitors in a courteous, professional, and compassionate manner. Answer telephone calls promptly, directing calls appropriately, taking accurate messages, and responding to enquiries in accordance with practice procedures. Triage patients appropriately, book appointments, process requests for home visits, and provide information and guidance as required. Keep patients informed of any delays or changes to appointments and deal with concerns in a calm and professional manner. Register new patients, ensuring all registration forms are completed correctly and patient records are created and updated accurately. Handle patient complaints sensitively and in accordance with the practice complaints procedure, escalating concerns where appropriate. Ensure reception and waiting areas remain clean, tidy, and welcoming. Support the Prescriptions Team by advising patients of the practice's 72-hour turnaround time for repeat prescription requests. Follow all reception, administrative, and practice protocols and procedures. Ensure hospital and laboratory courier collection procedures are followed correctly. Inform patients of private and non-NHS service charges, process payments, and issue receipts where appropriate. Open and close the practice as required, ensuring the security of the premises and setting or disabling alarms in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain the highest standards of patient confidentiality and comply with all information governance, GDPR, and confidentiality requirements at all times. title: Administrative Assistant (12 Month Maternity Cover)

Process Subject Access Requests, insurance reports, solicitor requests, DVLA forms and other patient information requests. Support the practice complaints process and Zero Tolerance Policy. Liaise with external organisations, contractors and IT providers. Complete audits and ensure compliance with NHS and practice policies. Provide flexible reception and administrative cover to support the wider team and deliver an excellent patient service. The Administrative Assistant is responsible for undertaking a wide range of administrative and secretarial duties and providing comprehensive administrative support to the multidisciplinary team. This includes the timely processing of both electronic and paper based information, liaising with internal staff and external organisations, including secondary care providers and community services, and working in accordance with current practice policies and procedures, including the use of the Electronic Referral Service (ERS). The post holder will also coordinate the practice complaints procedure and oversee the Zero Tolerance Policy, ensuring all processes are managed efficiently and in accordance with NHS guidance. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrative Assistant. From time to time, additional duties may be required depending on workload and staffing levels. The Administrative Assistant will: a. Act as the complaints lead, ensuring all complaints are managed promptly and in accordance with the NHS Complaints Procedure. b. Manage the practice Zero Tolerance Policy. c. Process requests for information, including Subject Access Requests (SARs), insurance reports, solicitor requests and DVLA medical reports. Raise invoices where applicable and prepare medical reports from patient records. d. Manage Primary Care Support England (PCSE) processes, including: Patient deductions New registrations Patient amendments FP69 forms Notespace management Processing incoming and outgoing medical records Liaising with PCSE as required e. Maintain and file patient medical records in alphabetical order and undertake photocopying as required. f. Support the Senior Administrator by liaising with external providers regarding maintenance issues and updating relevant logs, including: Building maintenance Information Technology systems Telephone systems g. Support the Senior Receptionist in managing the practice email inbox, ensuring emails are actioned within three working days. h. Support the Senior Receptionist with prescription processing and provide cover during periods of absence. i. Complete all tasks within the Reception and personal inboxes on a daily basis. j. Manage the new patient registration email inbox and ensure all required documentation is received. k. Register new and temporary patients and accurately enter patient information onto the clinical system. l. Process change of address requests and remove patients who move outside the practice boundary. m. Scan and accurately attach patient documentation to electronic medical records on a daily basis. n. Support the Senior Administrator by contacting patients on behalf of the practice as required. o. Process patient online access applications. p. Manage the 24 hour Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitor (ABPM) waiting list, arrange appointments and ensure appropriate follow up. q. Lead the monthly Childhood Immunisation recall programme, ensuring eligible children receive three invitations where appropriate. r. Manage recall programmes for: Vitamin B12 injections High Risk Diabetes reviews Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) monitoring s. Lead the practice cancer referral failsafe process using C the Signs software. t. Process all incoming GP2GP tasks. u. Process Summary Care Record updates and resolve any related errors. v. Support the Reception Team in arranging hospital transport for patients attending their first outpatient appointment. w. Carry out general reception administration duties to support the Reception Team. x. Monitor and maintain the reception area, patient notice boards and information leaflets. y. Manage the cervical screening deferral process. z. Complete routine practice audits, including: Fire extinguisher checks (monthly) First aid box checks (quarterly) Vaccine fridge monitoring (weekly) Inventory checks (quarterly) Defibrillator checks (daily) aa. Manage the blood pressure machine loan service, ensuring equipment is issued, monitored and returned. bb. Complete monthly audits for patients prescribed high risk medicines, ensuring blood tests are completed when due, maintaining the monitoring spreadsheet and escalating concerns to the Senior Clinical Pharmacist. cc. Run weekly and monthly safeguarding Did Not Attend (DNA) reports and action patients in accordance with the practice safeguarding policy. The Administrative Assistant will also undertake Medical Secretary duties, including: a. Typing letters, reports and other clinical documentation as required. b. Liaising with hospitals, community services and other external organisations to ensure referrals are processed efficiently. c. Processing referrals to secondary care using the Electronic Referral Service (ERS) and secure NHS email. d. Reviewing and actioning all ERS workflow tasks on a daily basis. e. Contacting hospital departments by email and processing responses. f. Managing administrative enquiries efficiently and professionally. g. Processing patient calling letters as requested. h. Answering incoming telephone calls, transferring calls where appropriate or dealing with enquiries directly. i. Managing administrative queries from patients and healthcare professionals. j. Running clinical system searches as requested. k. Maintaining a clean, organised and efficient working environment. l. Providing administrative support to all members of the clinical team. m. Managing the C the Signs cancer failsafe process and ensuring appropriate patient follow up. In addition to the duties above, the Administrative Assistant may also be required to: a. Support the Senior Receptionist with reception duties, providing cover during staff absences and assisting with opening and closing procedures. b. Support the Senior Administrator with additional administrative duties and deputise in their absence where required. c. Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role, as requested by the Practice Manager.

title: Medical Receptionist & Administrator
description: Burney Street Practice is looking for a friendly, organised and motivated Medical Receptionist & Administrator to join our busy and supportive GP practice team. This is a varied role combining front-of-house patient services with essential administrative duties. You will be one of the first points of contact for our patients, both face-to-face and over the telephone, and will work closely with our clinical and administrative teams to help ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Previous GP practice or healthcare experience would be an advantage; however, we also welcome applications from candidates with strong reception, customer service or administrative experience who are enthusiastic, quick to learn and keen to develop within General Practice. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys working with people, thrives in a busy and varied environment and would like to become a valued member of an established primary care team. The role involves providing a friendly, efficient reception and administrative service to patients, visitors and the wider practice team. Main duties include welcoming and assisting patients, answering telephone calls, managing appointments, responding to queries and signposting patients to the appropriate clinician or service. Administrative responsibilities include processing correspondence, scanning and filing documents, updating patient records and registrations, supporting patient recalls and QOF work, and completing tasks delegated by clinical and non-clinical colleagues. The successful candidate will work across both practice sites and will need to be organised, flexible and able to manage a varied workload in a busy General Practice environment. Job Description The successful candidate will work across both Reception and Administration, providing an effective and efficient service to patients, colleagues and other healthcare professionals. Your responsibilities will include: Welcoming patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and courteous manner Answering incoming telephone calls and dealing with patient enquiries Booking, amending and cancelling appointments in accordance with practice procedures Helping and signposting patients to the most appropriate clinician or healthcare service Responding to patient queries and providing accurate information Processing repeat prescription requests and directing queries appropriately Handling requests for home visits in accordance with practice protocols Maintaining a clean, tidy and professional reception area Supporting the opening and closing of the practice when required You will also undertake a range of administrative duties, including: Processing incoming and outgoing correspondence Scanning, filing and maintaining accurate patient records Processing new and temporary patient registrations Updating patient information on EMIS Web Monitoring and completing administrative tasks Supporting patient call and recall work, including QOF and long-term condition care Processing administrative requests and documentation Supporting clinical and non-clinical colleagues with delegated administrative tasks Attending staff meetings and contributing to service improvements The duties are varied, and the successful candidate will undertake a range of responsibilities depending on the needs of the practice.

title: Practice Administrator
description: We are recruiting for part time administrator at our practice based in Clapham, SW4. This is for maternity leave cover with a minimum of 9 months contract which may be extended up to 1 year. The successful applicant must be able to start mid October and must have experience of managing SARS/Insurance reports/DWP forms etc. 12 hours per week- 4 hours per day to be worked between 9am-5pm. Working days will be Monday/Wednesday & Friday Hourly Rate: £14.80 per hour. The successful applicant will be an integral part of our Primary Care team, supporting the delivery of high standard patient care. As the first point of contact for our patients and and outside agencies, they will have excellent customer service skills, experience and/or an excellent understanding of managing medical reports, SARS and letter requests from outside agencies- Solicitors/DWP/Insurance companies- & our patients and the associated processes. Managing all aspects of Medical Reports/SARS/Private letters and forms Managing the IGPR system and software Liaising with patients and practice staff in relation to the above Ordering supplies for the practice- medical, stationery, toners. Providing support to our administrator and reception team as required. The successful candidate will be required to be flexible, providing cover for annual leave and sick leave. PREVIOUS APPLICANTS NEED NOT APPLY The key responsibilities for this role are: Assisting our Registration Clerk with the processing of online registrations RESPONSIBLE TO: Assistant Practice Manager The primary role of the practice administrator is to manage requests made to the practice for Medical Reports and SARS requests, in addition to these duties, the post holder will be required to provide urgent cover for our registration administrator as directed by the Assistant Practice Manager. The post holder must have an excellent understanding of Access to Medical Records and Data protection. In addition, excellent IT skills are required and experience of using IGPR software is desired but not essential. It is important that all members of staff are prepared to take on additional duties or relinquish existing duties to maintain efficient running of the practice and changes in how services are provided. The Partners reserve the right to redistribute duties and functions among members of staff from time to time and requests for such changes shall not be reasonably refused. Duties and Responsibilities Managing and processing requests for Medical Reports and SARS requests Ensure upon receipt of requests for SARS and Medical Reports, all details are logged onto spreadsheet and reviewing and updating accordingly. Responsible for processing requests within specific time frames & following correct process. Manage requests for completion of private forms and requests for letters. Including discussing fees with both patients and clinicians. Manage requests from outside agencies for reports such as Child Protection/ Police Manage and maintain the IGPR data and software. Be the liaison between insurance companies and patients in relation viewing reports prior to sending. Responsible for redacting record entries relating to SARS and liaise with clinicians as required. First point of contact for patients in relation to requests and queries relating to private letters/completion forms Managing and responding to tasks sent by reception & clinical team in a timely manner. Ordering supplies: Responsible for the ordering of stationery, medical and IT supplies, ensuring stock is managed effectively and storeroom well maintained. . Other Duties : Provide cover in the absence of the registration administrator, ensuring all online registrations via Health Tec1 software, are processed, as required and instructed by the Assistant Practice Manager. Education Attend practice meetings. Attend suitable educational courses outside the practice. Attend training sessions within the practice. Complete mandatory Practice Index modules as required Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Actively reporting of health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general/patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Demonstrate due regard for safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner that is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, with such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate This job description will be reviewed at your regular staff appraisal. PERSON SPECIFICATION Essential Desirable Excellent IT skills including Excel/ Word Working knowledge of EMIS Excellent Knowledge of Data Protection and Access to Medical Records Working knowledge of Docman/Accurx Aptitude to learn new software & processes Working knowledge of IGPR software Excellent time management & organisational skills Previous experience of working within the NHS Excellent customer service skills Knowledge of NHS registration processes Ability to work autonomously and as part of a team. Excellent communication skills both written and verbal It is the policy of Hetherington Group Practice that no job applicant or employee shall receive less favourable treatment than another on the grounds of sex, marital status, age, disability, race, religion, creed, colour, national origin or sexual orientation. This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. You must therefore disclose all spent and unspent convictions, cautions, reprimands and final warnings. If you are offered the post we will need to obtain a satisfactory DBS disclosure for you.

Join Elysium Healthcare as an Incident Reporting Administrator and play a key role in supporting and improving our incident management and patient safety reporting systems. In this rewarding role, you will be responsible for supporting the development, maintenance and continuous improvement of Elysium's Incident Management System (IMS), ensuring it enables the safe, effective and compliant management of patient safety events. Your key responsibilities include developing and maintaining the Incident Management System (IMS), ensuring compliance with healthcare frameworks, and aligning the system with operational needs. Are you passionate about patient safety, governance and using data to drive meaningful improvements in healthcare? Join Elysium Healthcare as an Incident Reporting Administrator and play a key role in supporting and improving our incident management and patient safety reporting systems. In this rewarding role, you will be responsible for supporting the development, maintenance and continuous improvement of Elysium's Incident Management System (IMS), ensuring it enables the safe, effective and compliant management of patient safety events. Working closely with clinical teams, governance leads, IT colleagues and external stakeholders, you will help ensure the system aligns with operational requirements and national healthcare frameworks, including PSIRF, LFPSE and MHSDS. You will act as a vital link between technology and clinical practice, translating clinical, operational and regulatory requirements into clear and actionable system improvements. By engaging with users across the organisation, you will identify opportunities to enhance system performance, improve user experience and support the ongoing development of incident reporting processes. A key aspect of the role involves monitoring system usage, reviewing performance data and analysing feedback to identify trends and areas for improvement. You will develop and maintain reporting dashboards, produce meaningful insights and support the creation of KPIs that help track incident trends, reporting quality, system effectiveness and user engagement. Key Accountabilities: Leadership: Maintain a prioritised backlog/enhancement requests, ensuring features align with business goals and regulatory obligations. Collaborate with clinical and operational leaders to ensure the IMS supports real-world patient safety processes. Ensure usability for frontline staff and integration with investigation workflows such as RCA, After Action Reviews, and Learning from Deaths. Ensure the system meets NHS requirements, including compliance with the Patient Safety Incident Response Framework (PSIRF). Lead the implementation and maintenance of integration with LFPSE (Learn from Patient Safety Events) platform, including automated data submission and classification standards. Work with IT and development teams to ensure secure, scalable architecture. Oversee integrations with Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems, reporting tools, and identity management (e.g., Active Directory). Work within an ITIL framework by aligning product value delivery with IT service management processes, ensuring service stability, compliance and quality are maintained. Embed security by design principles within all application lifecycle activities, ensuring alignment with organisational cyber security standards and regulatory compliance requirements, and actively partnering with Information Security to manage risk effectively. Add to this re IT lifecycle management activities. Act as a point of contact on a day-to-day perspective, overseeing tickets raised, vendor performance against agreed targets and SLAs. Support service delivery review meetings. Understand and educate vendor proposed releases/developments and ensure third parties work with EHC change enablement policy. Stakeholder Engagement & Business Change Management Act as the voice of users across clinical, IT, and compliance teams. Lead workshops, user testing, and support training team to support successful adoption. Manage stakeholder expectations and ensure alignment with digital strategies. To be successful in this role, you will need: Working knowledge of product improvements, including backlog/enhancement management, roadmap development and the ability to prioritise Working knowledge of patient safety processes (e.g., PSIRF, Duty of Candour, incident investigation) Understanding of LFPSE requirements and NHS data standards Familiarity with EHR systems (e.g. Carenotes, Epic), API
